summary: In Greek mythology, Isander (Isandrus; also Peisander) is a Lycian prince, son of Bellerophon and Philonoe (daughter of Iobates). Homer says Ares slays him among the Solymi — misfortune balancing his father's earlier victories. Brother of Hippolochus (father of Glaucus) and Laodamia (mother of Sarpedon by Zeus).

sections.heading: Son of Bellerophon
paragraphs: After Bellerophon overcomes the Chimera and Iobates' trials, he weds the king's daughter — Philonoe, or in variants Alkimedousa, Anticleia, Pasandra, or Cassandra — and begets Isander, Hippolochus, and Laodamia (also Deidamia or Hippodamia).
Through Hippolochus the Lycian command at Troy descends to Glaucus; through Laodamia, Zeus fathers Sarpedon. Isander is the brother who does not live to send a son to the war.

sections.heading: Slain by Ares
paragraphs: Homer's Iliad (Book 6) recalls that Ares killed Isander as he fought the glorious Solymi, while Artemis of the golden reins slew Laodamia in anger — the gods cutting down Bellerophon's children after the hero's own fall from favour.
The atlas id isander-lycian is this Bellerophontid alone. Peisander is sometimes an alternate name for the same figure, not a second Lycian brother in this stemma.
